title: Balcony Solar in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin stopped paying for balcony solar.** SolarPLUS reopened on **8 January 2026** as SolarPLUS S and L with a 13 million euro budget, and the plug-in module was dropped. IBB Business Team says Steckersolargeraete are no longer funded because they now pay for themselves.

**The rules are simple now.** 800 watts at the inverter, 2,000 watt peak of module, one device per household. Since 16 May 2024 you tell nobody but the Marktstammdatenregister, within a month. Since 1 December 2025 the DIN VDE V 0126-95 standard allows a normal Schuko plug up to **960 watt peak** of module.

**An 800 watt peak kit in Berlin makes 595 kWh a year flat against a south railing**, 415 facing east, 403 facing west and only **153 facing north**. Laid back at 30 degrees facing south it reaches **810 kWh**, the best case in the city. Modelled with PVGIS on a clean, unshaded sky.

**Only what you use at that moment is money.** Your surplus leaves the flat unpaid. A flat drawing 130 watts in the background keeps **306 of those 595 kWh**, which at 37.93 cents is **116 euro a year** and pays a 400 euro kit back in about three and a half years.

**Buying more panel mostly buys you nothing.** Same south railing, 2,000 watt peak instead of 800: production jumps to 1,318 kWh, but the same flat keeps only 379 and saves **144 euro instead of 116**. Unless somebody is home in the day, the extra glass is a gift to the grid.

**Angle beats direction.** A north balcony with the panels laid back at 30 degrees keeps **323 kWh a year, more than a south balcony with the panels bolted flat to the railing**. Vertical panels also beat tilted ones in November, December and January, when you actually use the power.

**Your landlord can no longer refuse on looks.** Since early October 2024 a plug-in device is a privileged measure in the BGB, and Berlin asks for no building permit. Listed buildings still need the district Denkmalbehoerde, and shading from the building across the courtyard beats every number above.
